name: Jair Bolsonaro
summary: A former army captain and long-serving federal deputy, Bolsonaro governed Brazil as a right-wing nationalist who combined market reform and privatisation with strongly conservative positions on family, religion, guns and policing. His record also includes confrontation with the Supreme Court and the electoral system, and in 2025 the Supreme Court convicted him of plotting a coup to stay in power after losing the 2022 election.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: His government encouraged police use of lethal force and sought leniency for officers convicted of killings, the opposite of abolishing police.

abortion-legal.rationale: His administration put new barriers on legal abortion, such as ordering health workers to report rape survivors seeking abortion to police, and fired officials who backed safe abortion services.

central-planning.rationale: He described socialism in Venezuela as leaving everyone poor and deprived of freedom and said Brazil was pulled back from the brink of socialism.

close-ties-china.rationale: He described a comprehensive partnership launched with the United States in all areas as the centre of his foreign agenda, ahead of visits to China.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Supreme Court found him guilty of attempting to violently abolish democracy and trying to illegally retain power after losing an election.

death-penalty.rationale: In 2013 he said he supported execution for premeditated killing; in 2018 he said he would not push for it only because it would not pass, preferring life imprisonment.

decide-locally.rationale: He filed Supreme Court petitions to strike down state governors' decrees imposing social distancing, which the court rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: He called the Sao Paulo Forum a criminal organisation that must be fought and described the Cuban and Venezuelan governments as dictatorships his government worked against.

democracy-best.rationale: The Supreme Court convicted him in 2025 of attempting to keep power after losing the 2022 election and of organising a coup, an act contrary to accepting the voters' choice.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Human Rights Watch reports his government weakened environmental enforcement, deforestation reached its highest level since 2006 and the climate pledge was reduced.

economic-freedom.rationale: He told the General Assembly there can be no political freedom without economic freedom, and vice versa.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He told the UN that foreign pressure over the Amazon, including proposed sanctions, was disrespect of Brazilian sovereignty and that any help must fully respect it.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: He is reported to oppose racial quotas in universities, saying they mostly benefit well-off black students, while promising to keep socio-economic quotas.

free-trade.rationale: He said his government dropped Brazil's protectionist tradition and adopted trade liberalisation as a key tool for growth, concluding the Mercosur-EU and Mercosur-EFTA agreements.

gender-social-construct.rationale: He ordered the education ministry to draft a ban on what he calls gender ideology in schools and amplified the campaign against gender education.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: He titled no indigenous territory during his term and his agency halted demarcation processes, after pledging not to designate one more centimetre.

legalize-drugs.rationale: He signed a law allowing compulsory internment of drug users in treatment facilities without prior judicial authorisation, a prohibitionist policy.

limit-growth.rationale: His government advanced bills easing environmental licensing and opening indigenous territories to mining and agribusiness, favouring growth over environmental limits.

limit-guns.rationale: He loosened gun law by decree in January and May 2019, ending the requirement to justify a need and raising ammunition limits.

local-essentials-public.rationale: He highlighted the concession of water distribution and sewage services in Rio de Janeiro to private operators as the largest sanitation auction in the sector's history.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: His government signed the law allowing the state power utility Eletrobras to be privatised, moving a major enterprise from public to market control.

military-guardian-role.rationale: In 2020 he argued to his ministers that Article 142 of the constitution lets any branch call in the armed forces to restore order between branches.

more-religion-public.rationale: He appointed a pastor to the Supreme Court after promising a 'terribly evangelical' justice and keeps religious services and pastors at the presidential palace.

nation-first.rationale: His campaign and inaugural commitment was to put Brazil above everything, and he told the UN that foreign pressure over the Amazon had to respect Brazilian sovereignty.

national-rebirth.rationale: He called on Congress to restore and rebuild the homeland, freeing it from corruption, crime, economic irresponsibility and ideological submission, and presented a new Brazil emerging from the brink of socialism.

national-resource-control.rationale: He told the UN that the Amazon is not humankind's heritage, that Brazil's resources are its own and that any environmental aid must fully respect Brazilian sovereignty.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: In his inaugural speech he promised to value the family, respect religions and the Judeo-Christian tradition, and conserve the country's values.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: He stressed that the 2022 fall in fuel and energy prices came from tax rationalisation and not from price-fixing or other state intervention.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: He said Brazil worked with the United States and others to restore democracy in Venezuela and to preserve and promote democracy in Latin America.

property-fundamental.rationale: At Davos he pledged to protect the right to life and to private property.

public-ownership.rationale: He signed the 2021 law enabling the privatisation of Eletrobras, one of the country's largest state companies, against keeping major industries public.

reduce-immigration.rationale: His government left the UN migration compact and deported border-violating arrivals, yet maintained and expanded Operation Welcome for Venezuelans and left immigration regularisation in place.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He presented his government's course as deregulation and streamlined bureaucracy to reduce the burden on business, and later cited an economic freedom law.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: His agency allowed private land claims to be registered inside indigenous areas awaiting demarcation, a measure courts suspended as an invitation to invade.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He said families are only those made of a man and a woman, a statement reported by Human Rights Watch in 2019.

separate-church-state.rationale: He publicly promised and then appointed a 'terribly evangelical' Presbyterian pastor to the Supreme Court and holds religious services at the presidential palace.

separated-powers.rationale: Human Rights Watch reports he harassed the Supreme Court, asked the Senate to impeach a justice and said he would not obey a justice's decisions.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: He ordered a health booklet for adolescents on pregnancy and infections withdrawn and acted to keep comprehensive sexuality education from children.

social-market-economy.rationale: He pairs market reform, privatisation and concessions with a large emergency income programme in 2020 and the Auxilio Brasil minimum-income programme, as he described them to the UN.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: His 2019 decrees widened civilian purchase of firearms and ammunition and let some lower-ranking military members carry, while his camp pushed to widen carrying by civilians.

suppress-opposition.rationale: His administration pursued prison sentences against at least 17 critics, including under a military-era security law, though many cases were later closed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He said his administration put protectionism behind it, and in 2022 cited tariff cuts to zero on thousands of products.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: In a 1999 television interview he said he favoured torture, applying it to a banker who refused to testify to a congressional inquiry.

traditional-family.rationale: He told the UN that the traditional nuclear family is the very foundation of civilization and that Brazil has the family as its foundation.

turn-back-illegal-migrants.rationale: His government ordered the deportation of people who entered Brazil in violation of pandemic border restrictions, even where they intended to seek asylum.

notes: Mature position taken from his time as president (2019-2022) and the record of that term, with his congressional career (1991-2018) and the 1999 interviews counted only where the presidency left no record. Several statements were left null because the sources opened do not settle them: the official texts of the gun decrees, the 2019 Economic Freedom Act and the pension amendment could not be opened (planalto.gov.br returned only its home page to every download agent, and the Wayback copy rendered empty), so those answers rest on press and Human Rights Watch reports of the record at medium confidence. Themes searched: economy and privatisation, trade, guns and policing, indigenous land, environment, abortion and family, gender education, religion, race quotas, immigration, courts, elections and the coup case, foreign policy (UN speeches 2019-2022). Not searched: his Chamber of Deputies speeches and votes (no local corpus for the Brazilian Chamber), the 2018 government programme as filed with the electoral court, and his 2018 campaign debates. His statements that the dictatorship was glorious or that torture is acceptable date from the 1990s to 2016 and are used only for the torture statement, where he left no record. The September 2025 conviction is under appeal and is used as a court finding reported by the press, not as an established fact.
